title: There Was an Old Lady Who Swallowed Some Books!
author: Lucille Colandro

demand_candidate.rationale: Cumulative school-themed structure is highly suitable for AAC prediction, sequencing, repeated participation, and concrete icon vocabulary.

hero.name: The Old Lady
hero.description: Recurring cheerful, bug-eyed, big-mouthed cartoon old lady from the Colandro/Jared Lee series who swallows increasingly strange objects; in this book she is shown swallowing school supplies before popping out a backpack.
hero.source_note: Generic 'old woman' Boardmaker icons won't match this specific series' distinctive cartoon illustration style (bug-eyed, big-mouthed, cheerful) that children recognise from the book cover — recommend sourcing a clip-art image matching the Jared Lee illustration style or a close cartoon-old-lady equivalent from TPT/Creative Fabrica.

ambiguous.reason: This book, like the whole series, centers on the old lady swallowing objects — the action meaning, not the bird, is correct here

ambiguous.reason: In context it's the last small school-supply item she swallows before the backpack pops out, so a school-supply-style bag image is most accurate

book_summary: In this back-to-school entry in Colandro's cumulative 'Old Lady' rhyme series, the old lady swallows a stack of books, then a pen, a pencil case, a ruler, a folder, some chalk, and a bag, one after another in classic 'I don't know why' fashion. The twist ending reveals she's been swallowing school supplies on purpose: when the yellow school bus arrives, she cheers and out pops a brand-new backpack, ready for the first day of school.

fringe_justifications.books: The title item — the old lady's very first swallow of the story, a stack of books, kicking off the cumulative rhyme.
fringe_justifications.pen: One of the school supplies she swallows in sequence, part of the list confirmed as pen, pencil case, ruler, folder, chalk, and a bag.
fringe_justifications.pencil case: The second item swallowed after books, part of the escalating list of school supplies in the story.
fringe_justifications.ruler: A specific swallowed item in the sequence, listed among the school items she gobbles up on each page turn.
fringe_justifications.folder: A specific swallowed item in the sequence, appearing between the ruler and the chalk in her list of gulps.
fringe_justifications.chalk: A specific swallowed item in the sequence, tying to the classroom/school supply theme just before the bag.
fringe_justifications.bag: The final small item she swallows before the story's twist reveal, right before the bus arrives and backpack pops out.
fringe_justifications.backpack: The surprise pay-off of the whole story — when the bus appears she cheers and a brand-new backpack pops out, resolving why she swallowed everything.
fringe_justifications.bus: The big yellow school bus arriving is the story's climax and the moment that explains the old lady's plan all along.
fringe_justifications.school: The entire book is framed around the first day of school, with the old lady swallowing supplies to be ready for it.
fringe_justifications.swallow: The core repeated action of the entire 'Old Lady' series — she swallows something new on every single page, driving the cumulative structure.

grounding_note: Confirmed via multiple retailer/library sources (Scholastic Book Clubs, Barnes & Noble, Goodreads, Internet Archive) that this 2012 Colandro/Jared Lee title has the old lady swallowing books, a pen, a pencil case, a ruler, a folder, chalk, and a bag, then popping out a backpack when the school bus arrives — a back-to-school twist on the classic 'Swallowed a Fly' rhyme. Reviews independently corroborate the same item sequence and ending, so plot details are well-corroborated across sources.
